fieldsRead.text: This English-taught TU/e degree studies software systems and web services through programming, mathematical reasoning, algorithms, data and computer systems. It combines taught foundations with engineering projects, professional development and an individual final research project.

The first UCR programme emphasises software, networks, algorithms and computational engineering applications. The second gives more weight to mathematical models, statistical learning and empirical methods. Both offer related computer-science capacities, with gaps in dedicated computer architecture, technical security, formal software specification and TU/e’s compulsory engineering-project sequence.

One of three capstones is shown, selected by official order. Places are limited. Elective choices and project topics require the applicable approval and prior knowledge; current offerings and requirements may change.

45 EC of elective choice: at most 15 EC at introductory level and at least 15 EC at advanced level, with no content overlap. Submit the planned programme for examination-board approval after earning 90 EC; changes require renewed approval. No fixed elective package is assumed.
One 5-EC capstone is required. This example uses Heuristic Algorithms; places are limited and registration is first come, first served.

This 10-EC course spans quarters 1–2 and combines software-engineering study with a real-customer team project. Software Specification normally precedes entry; the displayed sequence meets this. The current course page requires enrolment by 15 July; check the applicable year’s deadline.

This required 10-EC individual research project spans quarters 3–4. Entry requires 120 EC, all compulsory first-year courses and the applicable computer-science credits and topic preparation. The displayed prior-major sequence meets the stated 95-EC computer-science requirement.

The normal first-year study-advice threshold is 45 of 60 EC, with applicable personal circumstances considered. SCOP/e and Alumni Night, at least five Studium Generale activities and MyFuture activities with a total value of seven are additional completion requirements; they do not add credits to the 180 EC shown.

TU/e CSE includes dedicated Computer Systems, Automata and Formal Languages, Software Specification, Operating Systems, Security, autonomous-systems and multidisciplinary CBL courses, a compulsory 10-EC Software Engineering project, a choice of advanced capstone and a 10-EC individual research-oriented Bachelor Final Project. UCR offers substantial programming, databases, systems, algorithms, mathematics, data science and AI, but neither alternative reproduces that complete engineering and project sequence. TU/e also preserves 45 EC of genuine elective space.

Combine programming, software construction, relational databases, networks and operating systems with algorithms, mathematical foundations, data and learning methods. Robotics and linear-system modelling add computational engineering applications. User-oriented product methods and general philosophical, ethical and communication work complement the computing core. Dedicated computer architecture, technical security, formal software specification and the full compulsory engineering-project sequence remain gaps.

Combine programming, software development, databases and algorithms with advanced calculus, linear systems, numerical analysis, probability, machine learning and reinforcement-learning agents. Empirical research and experimental-statistics courses place additional weight on model evaluation and quantitative inquiry; their project topics are not necessarily computing. This is a mathematical and statistical direction within computing, with less network and systems-engineering breadth.
